messages:

Subject: Initial evidence request for DPA / DPIA review

Hi Marcus,

Acme is moving into a short procurement window and our privacy team needs a compact evidence pack to complete a DPIA and verify contractual controls before we finalize the DPA addendum. Can Redwood provide the following artifacts within the next two weeks?

- Processing ledger (GDPR Art. 30) covering June 2024 – present (CSV preferred)
- Current subprocessor manifest and onboarding dates
- Summary of audit rights and how remote audits are handled (SOC2 reports acceptable; what additional records can be shared)
- DPIA support: sample questionnaire responses and redacted operational artifacts that show mitigations for data subject rights / retention
- Data transfers: legal basis for transfers, SCCs if applicable, and a list of regions where customer data may be egressed
- Retention/erasure runbook or sample logs showing deletion workflows for test tenant(s)

Attached is our DPIA questionnaire to help scope what we’ll need. If your team cannot share any of the above, please indicate the appropriate redaction or process (e.g., view-only Drive, auditor liaison). We may request a short call with your compliance team.

Thanks in advance — can you confirm receipt and an estimated delivery date?

Best,
Alicia Torres
Legal Ops — Acme Energy

Hi Alicia / Marcus,

Thanks for the heads-up, Marcus. Alicia — I’m Kim from Redwood’s Security & Compliance team; I’ll coordinate the DPIA artifacts and processing evidence. A few notes on scope and how we typically respond so you can plan:

1) Processing ledger (Art. 30):
   - We can provide a CSV export (redwood_processing_ledger_art30.csv) with the processing activities, data categories, and subprocessors for the requested period.

2) Subprocessors / transfers:
   - The attached manifest contains our current subcontractors and onboarding dates. For cross-border transfers we rely on SCCs where required; we will include a short transfer map and redaction-friendly wording for public-facing materials.

3) Audit rights and evidence access:
   - Standard approach: SOC2 report plus curated artifact package. For customers requiring deeper access, we offer a remote, recorded evidence review with a designated compliance liaison. On-site audits are handled under a signed audit process addendum and typically require a separate schedule.

4) DPIA support & retention logs:
   - We can provide redacted runbook excerpts and sample retention/erasure logs from a synthetic tenant to demonstrate workflows. For DPIA questionnaire responses, I’ll populate answers and flag items that require legal/contractual gating.

5) Sensitive artifacts & third-party reviewers:
   - If Acme needs unredacted artifacts, we require an NDA or an auditor contract. We can also host a secure screening session where a member of our security team walks through live artifacts.

Next steps I’ll take today: upload the processing ledger CSV and a short evidence index to a secure Drive folder and share a view-only link with Acme. I’ll also draft answers to your attached questionnaire and tag open items for legal.

I’ve attached the processing ledger now. If this looks like what you need, we can confirm the call times Marcus proposed and I’ll book a slot.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
